svg.title: Manual route on the communicator, mockups
svg.text: Manual route and Neighbors · communicator
T-LoRa Pager, 480×222, drawn at 2×. Turn moves, press selects, Backspace goes back. Modeled on the iOS manual path.
Route
The Route screen gains Edit route. While a manual route is held, the route names it, and Clear manual route takes Reset route's place.
1 · Route, learned
Edit route sits between Confirmed and Reset route. It opens the editor seeded with the route shown; with nothing learned, the
editor starts with only You and the peer.
2 · Route, manual route held
The header reads Manual. Then flood and Held join Confirmed. Held counts down instead of naming a time, so it needs no clock.
Clear manual route returns to the learned route, or to flooding, without asking.
3 · Peer, manual route held
The peer's Route row and the conversation header say Manual too, so a held route is never a surprise.
Editor
One screen, the iOS editor's rows in one list. Turn walks the hops, then the rows below. You and the peer are fixed, so they are not stops.
4 · Edit route
Seeded from the learned route. Each hop is a stop. The grip says it moves. Add hop sits after the last repeater and goes away at
5 · A hop's menu
Press on a hop: Move or Remove. No confirmation; nothing is saved until Save.
6 · Moving a hop
Move lifts the hop. Turning carries it through the others; press puts it down, Backspace puts it back where it was.
7 · Then flood, changing
Press makes the value active; turning steps Off, 1 hop … 15 hops; press sets it. The rail past it is dashed while it is on. Hold for
works the same: 30 min, 1 hour, 4 hours, 12 hours, 1 day.
8 · Ping along route, then Save
Ping along route opens the Ping screen for the unsaved draft and comes back with its result in the row. Save holds the route from
now; Backspace returns to Route.
9 · A direct route
Every hop removed. The flood row reads Flood, counted from this device, and the route saves as direct.
10 · Leaving with changes
Backspace with unsaved changes asks. Without changes it just leaves.
Add hop
Add hop opens a list of candidates for the next hop. Choosing one appends it and moves on to the hop after it; Backspace returns to the editor with every hop added so far.
11 · Add hop, neighbors
What the previous hop last reported hearing, in the Neighbors row form (17), asked along the route so far; for hop 1, this device's
own list. Opening sends nothing. When the peer is among them, it pins to the top with Finish here, which ends the route.
12 · Add hop, further down
Load more and Refresh each send one request. Nodes already on the route are dimmed and say In path. Known repeaters
follow, most recently heard first.
13 · Add hop after a bare hint
A hop known only by its hint has no address to ask, so only Known repeaters are listed.
14 · Typing a router hint
Typing filters, as on every list. Four or more Base58 characters also offer the router hint they fix, with its hex. Enter adds the
tinted top result.
15 · A hint read two ways
“3D9F” is a Base58 prefix and also four hex digits, so both are offered, each labeled. A prefix that straddles two hints is offered
twice the same way.
While held
A held route is used for every send to the peer. A missed ack still falls back to one flood, and the route stays.
16 · Switch to the learned route?
After two sends in a row miss on the manual route while their floods are acknowledged (one, if this device moved far). Once per
saved route. Keep manual route stops asking until it is edited.
Neighbors
The repeaters one router reports hearing, a page at a time. Opening shows the last listing and sends nothing; every page is one exchange across the mesh.
17 · A repeater, Neighbors focused
Offered on any node that advertises repeating, whatever its role, and from a saved peer's page the same way.
18 · Neighbors
Name, then how the router heard each one: bars, RSSI and SNR, how long ago, and how far from the router when both placed
themselves. A known node opens its page, which has Neighbors too.
19 · Asking who a hint is
A bare hint shows the search glyph. Press asks it who it is, steered down the route to the router; the answer names it in place.
Bridged: heard over a link, not the air. Rows unheard for 6 hours fade.
20 · Refreshing
Load more asks for the page after the last one held; Refresh asks for the top again. Either spins in its own row, and the rows stay
until the answer replaces them.
21 · No answer

g.text: Out of reach, or it keeps no neighbor list

svg.text: The listing held stays. The line says why, and Refresh is focused, so a press asks again.
22 · Never read
Not read until Refresh. A router asked that lists nobody says None instead.
